raw_webpage_content:
Signs of strawberry ripening

As berries ripen, their color changes from pale green to mostly red, and the seeds remain visible on the fruit surface.

The change from pale green to red marks the transition from green fruit development to ripening. A berry is ready for picking when its skin is fully red and the flesh yields slightly to gentle pressure.

raw_webpage_content:
Flower development in strawberries

At the first-bloom stage, several flower buds have opened. Each open flower has five white petals surrounding a yellow center.

This marks the transition from visible flower buds to flowering.

raw_webpage_content:
Recognizing fruit set

During fruit set, the flower petals fade and fall. The green receptacle begins to swell while the green sepals remain visible.

The change from flowering to fruit set is marked by petals falling and the receptacle beginning to swell.
